{{nihongo|'''Iwaki Shrine'''|石城神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Suo Province]].

'''Iwaki Shrine'' (Iwaki Shrine) is located in {{ill|Yamaguchi Prefecture|Q127264|qid=Q127264}}{{ill|Hikari, Yamaguchi|Q823502|qid=Q823502}} Oaza Shioda. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old company rank}} is {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=Prefectural company|qid=Q90139226|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha}}.

It is located at the top of {{ill|Mount Iwaki (Yamaguchi)|Q11585424|qid=Q11585424}} (362 meters above sea level), which is known for {{ill|ancient mountain fortress in Japan|Q6431764|qid=Q6431764}}'s {{ill|Iwakisan Kōgoishi|Q18990554|qid=Q18990554}} (national {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}}).

== Enshrined God ==
The following three deities are currently enshrined. </ref>.
* {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|abstract|Q386563|az|Ooyamatsimu|de|Ōyamatsumi|fa|اویاماتسومی|fr|Ōyamatsumi|hr|O-Yama-Tsu-mi|ja|オオヤマツミ|ko|오야마쓰미노카미|mni|ꯑꯣꯌꯃꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|ru|Ооямацуми|simple|Ōyamatsumi|sv|Ōyamatsumi|tr|Ōyamatsumi|zh|大山津見|qid=Q386563|lt=Oyamazumi no Kami}} - The main deity.
* {{ill|Raijin|Q12808082|qid=Q12808082}} (Ikazuchinokami)
* {{ill|Kuraokami|Q644201|qid=Q644201|lt=Takaokamikami}}
In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, which was established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), there is one enshrined deity. In the past, the enshrined deity {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=honjibutsu}} was {{ill|Shakyamuni Tathāgata|Q11644537|qid=Q11644537}} for Oyamazumi, and {{jalink|Fugen Bosatsu|Q868306} for thunder god. }, {{ill|Manjushri|Q471696|qid=Q471696}} was enshrined in the Takaojin Shrine.{{Sfn|Ishiki Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1980}}

== History ==

== Founding ==
[[File:Iwaki-san Kogoishi, higashi-suimon.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Iwakisan Kōgoishi|Q18990554|qid=Q18990554}} (national {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}})}}]]
Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Ishiki Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1980}}. According to the shrine's legend, it was founded in the 3rd year of {{ill|Emperor Bidatsu|ar|الإمبراطور بيداتسو|arz|الامبراطور بيداتسو|azb|بیداتسو (ایمپیراتور)|cs|Bidacu|de|Bidatsu|es|Bidatsu Tennō|fa|امپراتور بیداتسو|fi|Bidatsu|fr|Bidatsu|id|Kaisar Bidatsu|it|Bidatsu|ja|敏達天皇|ka|ბიდაცუ|ko|비다쓰 천황|mr|बिदात्सु|nl|Bidatsu|pl|Bidatsu|pt|Bidatsu|ru|Император Бидацу|sh|Car Bidatsu|simple|Emperor Bidatsu|sl|Cesar Bidacu|sv|Bidatsu|th|จักรพรรดิบิดัตสึ|tl|Emperador Bidatsu|tr|Bidatsu|uk|Імператор Бідацу|uz|Imperator Bidatsu|vi|Thiên hoàng Bidatsu|yo|Emperor Bidatsu|zh|敏达天皇|zh_min_nan|Bidatu Thian-hông|zh_yue|敏達天皇|qid=Q316637}} ({{ill|574|Q32597|qid=Q32597}}?) when Tsushi of Kibitunkura came to this area and was given an imperial plaque of ``Ishijo Palace.''

At {{ill|Mount Iwaki (Yamaguchi)|Q11585424|qid=Q11585424}}, where Ishishiro Shrine is located, it is known that {{ill|Iwakisan Kōgoishi|Q18990554|qid=Q18990554}}, which is an {{ill|ancient mountain fortress in Japan|Q6431764|qid=Q6431764}}, was built. There is no mention of the Ishishiro Mountain Kamago Stone in the literature, and its functional period is not clear, but it is presumed that there was a connection between the shrine and the mountain castle, based on the shrine's name, ``Ishijo''. There is also a theory that the shrine outside the precincts, Uwanari Shrine, was originally the god of Mt. Ishishiro, and with the construction of the mountain castle, the gods Oyamazumi, Raijin, and Takashiro were solicited by the imperial court, and Ishishiro Shrine was built as the guardian deity of the mountain castle in place of Uwanari Shrine.{{Sfn|Ishiki Shrine (Gods)|2000}}

== Outline ==
In {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokukushi}}, {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan}} It is recorded that in the 9th year ({{ill|867|Q30347|qid=Q30347}}), the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} of ``Ishijo no Kami'' was promoted from the upper rank of upper fifth rank to lower rank of junior fourth rank {{Sfn|Ishijo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1980}}. Also, {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=extended}}5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmeicho}} is {{ill|Suō Province|cs|Provincie Suó|de|Provinz Suō|es|Provincia de Suō|fa|ولایت سوئو|fr|Province de Suō|gl|Provincia de Suō|id|Provinsi Suō|it|Suō (provincia)|ja|周防国|ko|스오국|lt|Suo žemė|nl|Suo (provincie)|pt|Província de Suō|ru|Суо (провинция)|simple|Suō Province|sk|Suó (provincia)|sr|Провинција Суо|tr|Suō (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Суо|uz|Suo viloyati|wuu|周防国|zh|周防國|zh_min_nan|Suô-kok|qid=Q1053037}}{{ill|Kumage District, Yamaguchi|Q1042808|qid=Q1042808|lt=Ishiki Shrine is listed in Kumage District}} and is listed as {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} {{Sfn|Ishiki Shrine (Heibonsha)|1980}}.

{{ill|Karoku|Q1194421|qid=Q1194421}} In March 3rd year ({{ill|1227|Q5407|qid=Q5407}}), in ``Suo Ishijogu Shinkan Kai'', we can see a dispute regarding the shrine {{Sfn|Ishijo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1980}}.{{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} In July of the first year ({{ill|1469|Q6566|qid=Q6566}}), the current main shrine was built by {{ill|Ōuchi Masahiro|Q8081786|qid=Q8081786}}. This main shrine was built by Yoshioki Ouchi|Q909270}} in {{ill|Eishō (Muromachi period)|Q1193577|qid=Q1193577}}11 ({{ill|1514|Q6204|qid=Q6204}}) and by {{ill|Meireki|Q1192766|qid=Q1192766}}2 ({{ill|1656|Q6982|qid=Q6982}}). link|Tsunahiro Mori|Q11547682}} and {{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}} in 10 years ({{ill|1798|Q7823|qid=Q7823}}) and by {{ill|Mōri Narifusa|Q11547649|qid=Q11547649}} respectively. In addition, in {{ill|Ansei|Q1327259|qid=Q1327259}}4 ({{ill|1857|Q7680|qid=Q7680}}), {{ill|Mōri Takachika|Q1088423|qid=Q1088423}} ​​built the worship hall and Jingoji Niomon (current Ishijo Shrine Zuishinmon).

In {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}, there was a belief that Mt. Ishishiro was a sacred mountain site, and it was called ``Ishijoyama Shikinai Sansha Daigongen'' {{Sfn|Ishijo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1980}}.After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern company rank system}} It was ranked as {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and was promoted to {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}} in {{ill|Taishō era|ar|فترة تايشو|br|Oadvezh Taishō|ca|Període Taishō|cs|Období Taišó|de|Taishō-Zeit|eo|Taiŝo-epoko|es|Era Taishō|et|Taishō ajastu|eu|Taishō aroa|fa|دوره تایشو|fi|Taishō-kausi|fr|Ère Taishō|he|תקופת טאישו|hi|ताइशो युग|hu|Taisó-kor|hy|Տայսյո|id|Zaman Taishō|it|Periodo Taishō|ja|大正|ko|다이쇼 시대|lt|Taišio laikotarpis|lv|Taišo periods|ml|തായ്ഷോ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Taishō|nl|Taishoperiode|no|Taishō-perioden|pl|Taishō (okres)|pt|Período Taishō|ro|Perioada Taishō|ru|Тайсё|sh|Taishō period|simple|Taishō era|sr|Таишо период|sv|Taishō|th|ยุคไทโช|tl|Panahong Taishō|tr|Taişo Dönemi|uk|Період Тайсьо|uz|Taishō davri|vi|Thời kỳ Đại Chính|zh|大正|zh_classical|大正 (年號)|zh_min_nan|Tāi-chèng|zh_yue|大正 (日本年號)|qid=Q329174}}2 ({{ill|1913|Q2080|qid=Q2080}})<ref name="Historic Book"/>{{Sfn|Ishiki Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1980}}. Additionally, on the west side of the shrine there used to be Ishishiro Sanshanain Jingoji Temple, {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}}, but it was abandoned in 1870|1980}}.

== God level ==
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jokan}} August 16, 9th year ({{ill|867|Q30347|qid=Q30347}}), from the top of the fifth rank to the bottom of the fourth rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'') - Written as ``Ishijogami.''

== Precincts ==
[[File:Iwaki-jinja (Hikari), honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (National Important Cultural Property)}}]]The current main shrine was built in the first year of {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} ({{ill|1469|Q6566|qid=Q6566}}) in the late {{ill|Muromachi period|ar|فترة موروماتشي|ast|Periodu Muromachi|bcl|Panahon nin Muromachi|bg|Муромачи|bn|মুরোমাচি যুগ|ckb|سەردەمی مرۆماچی|cs|Období Muromači|de|Muromachi-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Muromaĉi|es|Período Muromachi|eu|Muromachi aroa|fa|دوره موروماچی|fi|Muromachi-kausi|fr|Époque de Muromachi|gl|Período Muromachi|he|תקופת אשיקאגה|hu|Muromacsi-kor|id|Zaman Muromachi|it|Periodo Muromachi|ja|室町時代|ko|무로마치 시대|lt|Muromači laikotarpis|nl|Muromachiperiode|pl|Muromachi (okres)|pt|Período Muromachi|ru|Период Муромати|simple|Muromachi period|sk|Obdobie Muromači|sl|Obdobje Muromači|sr|Муромачи период|sv|Ashikaga|th|ยุคมูโรมาจิ|tl|Panahong Muromachi|tr|Muromachi Dönemi|uk|Період Муроматі|vi|Thời kỳ Muromachi|wuu|室町时代|zh|室町时代|zh_min_nan|Muromati sî-tāi|zh_yue|室町時代|qid=Q334845}}. It is a large corner-wooden {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|Q3193781|qid=Q3193781}} building. The structure is 3-ken in girder rows, 1-ken in the front, 2-ken in the back, and a gable, and the roof is shingled. Characteristics of the Muromachi period can be seen everywhere, such as the toad. Inside the building, the back room is the inner hall, and the front two rooms are the outer hall, with the inner hall being one step higher. This main shrine is designated as a national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}, along with one designated palace and two ridge plates.<ref name="Country designation"/><ref>[http://bunkazai.pref.yamaguchi.lg.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=20009&pid=ss&search_value=%E7%9F%B3%E5 %9F%8E%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE&loopcnt_b=0&loopcnt_m=0&loopcnt=0&shicyouson=&meisyou=&shitei=&kubun=&syurui=&jidai=&loopcnt= Main Hall of Ishiki Shrine] (Yamaguchi Prefecture homepage ``Cultural Properties of Yamaguchi Prefecture'', Overview of Cultural Properties). </ref><ref name="Hikari City"/>. Regarding the architectural style of the main shrine, there is a document that says it is ``Sumikiri Kasuga-zukuri'' <ref> "National Treasures and Important Cultural Properties Encyclopedia 11 Buildings Vol. 1" supervised by the Agency for Cultural Affairs (Mainichi Shimbunsha, 1998), p. 354</ref> and a document that says ``Front irimoya-zukuri, rear gable-zukuri, tsumui-zukuri'' <ref> [https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/157775 Cultural Heritage Online]</ref>, but both refer to essentially the same format. ``Sumiki-iri Kasuga-zukuri'' is a type of Kasuga-zukuri (a type of gabled shrine building with an eave attached to the front), in which a sumiki (a member that extends at a 45-degree angle to the main building) is inserted between the main building and the eave.To the west of the precincts, there was once Jingo-ji Temple, a Betto-ji temple {{Sfn|Ishiki Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1980}}. At the end of the Edo period, the headquarters of the {{ill|Second Kiheitai|Q11602283|qid=Q11602283}} was also located at Jingo-ji Temple, but Jingo-ji Temple was abandoned in 1870 and the hall was lost, and the remaining Nio-mon gate on the approach is now used as the Zuishin-mon Gate of Ishijo Shrine.

== Setsusha ==
[[File:Iwaki-jinja (Hikari), Suga-sha.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sugasha}}]]
There are the following two Sessue Shrines {{Sfn|Ishiki Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1980}}.
* Suga Shrine - Precinct Shrine.
* Uwanarisha - outside shrine.

== Cultural assets ==

== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ==
* Main shrine (1 attached palace, 2 ridge tags) (building)
*: On May 27, 1907, it was designated as a special protected building based on the {{ill|Ancient Temples and Shrines Preservation Law|Q11411552|qid=Q11411552}}, and in 1950, it was designated as a national important cultural property with the enactment of the {{ill|Cultural Properties Protection Law|Q1188502|qid=Q1188502}}. Attached properties were additionally designated on February 3, 1979 <ref name="Nationally designated">{{Nationally designated cultural properties database|102|3238|Ishiki Shrine Main Hall}}</ref><ref>[http://bunkazai.pref.yamaguchi.lg.jp/bunkazai/summary.asp?mid=20009&pid=ss&svalue=%E7%9 F%B3%E5%9F%8E%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE&bloop=0&mloop=0&floop=0&shicyouson=&meisyou=&shitei=&kubun=&syurui=&jidai=&loopcnt=&m_mode=&m_value=&m_loopcnt= Main Hall of Ishiki Shrine] (Yamaguchi Prefecture homepage ``Cultural Properties of Yamaguchi Prefecture'', Cultural Properties Directory). </ref><ref name="Hikari City">[https://www.city.hikari.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunka/bunkazaiitiran.html#kuni Designated Cultural Property > Ishiki Shrine Main Hall] (Hikari City homepage). </ref>.
